account_changes_january.reading: 66 of the 95 changes touch the two campaigns that spent, so most of the month's edits were on what delivered. Campaign 2 (traffic) was switched off and back on 4 times between 2026-01-26 and 2026-01-30 (8 status changes, each time back on within a minute), around its first delivery on 2026-01-27. The log shows 2 'Ad delivered' events: one is the January ad; the other is a second ad in Ad set 1 that has no row in call 7, so it logged a start but recorded no impressions. The other 28 events are set-up and status edits on 3 campaigns and 3 ad sets with no spend in either month, plus 4 account events.

what_didnt_work.item: Campaign 2 (traffic) was switched off and on 4 times in its first days
what_didnt_work.evidence: call 9: 8 'Campaign status updated' events (Active and Inactive) between 2026-01-26 and 2026-01-30, around its first delivery on 2026-01-27
what_didnt_work.next_step: Each switch interrupts delivery. Leave the next campaign running for at least a week before changing its status.

what_didnt_work.item: No link clicks from either campaign
what_didnt_work.evidence: call 3: 0 link clicks in December (4 impressions) and January (60 impressions)
what_didnt_work.next_step: Below the floor, so this is not proof the ad fails. Give one campaign enough budget to reach 10 link clicks before judging it.

surprises.meaning: That is why January's CPM looks low: cheap app-network impressions, none of which clicked.

surprises.evidence: call 3 (account level; December had one campaign): 2 post engagements, 2 page engagements, 2 video views in December
surprises.meaning: People watched or reacted without clicking. Too few to read; worth watching once spend is real.
